Report Errors in the PDF - support@careerscloud.in Copyright 2014-2026 @ AffairsCloud.com 16 Daily Content PDF NATIONAL AFFAIRS India Shipbuilding Investment Conclave 2026: MoPSW Launches Naukosh Portal; CSL Signs MoU with Damen Shipyards The Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways (MoPSW) organised the India Shipbuilding Investment Conclave 2026, a two-day programme held from 16 to 17 November 2026 in New Delhi, Delhi, to attract global investments and strengthen India’s shipbuilding and ship repair industry. • On 16 November 2026, Union Minister Sarbananda Sonowal, MoPSW, launched the Naukosh Digital Portal, while Cochin Shipyard Limited (CSL) signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with the Netherlands-based Damen Shipyards Group to explore cooperation in future shipbuilding projects. Exam Hints: ✓ Event: India Shipbuilding Investment Conclave 2026 ✓ Dates: November 16 to November 17, 2026 ✓ Organiser: MoPSW ✓ Venue: New Delhi, Delhi ✓ Portal Launched: Naukosh Digital Portal ✓ Developed By: Directorate General of Maritime Administration (DGMA) ✓ Key MoU: CSL and Damen Shipyards Group, Netherlands ✓ Greenfield Shipbuilding Clusters: 05, including Dugarajapatnam in AP; Kuchhadi in Gujarat; Dighi in Maharashtra; Kendrapada in Odisha and Thoothukudi in TN ✓ Projected Cluster Investment: Nearly USD 10 billion Key Highlights of Conclave: Participants: The conclave brought together representatives from 30 global shipyards, shipping companies, equipment manufacturers, banks, investors and diplomatic missions, along with Indian industry leaders. • Major Shipbuilders: HD Korea Shipbuilding & Offshore Engineering (HD KSOE), Samsung Heavy Industries, Hanwha Ocean, Fincantieri and Meyer Werft. • Shipping and Logistics Companies: Maersk, Mediterranean Shipping Company (MSC), CMA CGM, Mitsui O.S.K. Lines (MOL) and DP World. Financial Package: The conclave built on the Government of India’s USD 8 billion shipbuilding financial package, approved in 2025, to strengthen domestic shipbuilding capacity and attract investments. Greenfield Shipbuilding Clusters: Investment Opportunity: The Government of India (GoI) identified five proposed greenfield shipbuilding clusters with projected investment opportunities of nearly USD 10 billion. Proposed Locations: 1. Dugarajapatnam – Andhra Pradesh (AP) 2. Kuchhadi – Gujarat 3. Dighi – Maharashtra 4. Kendrapada – Odisha 5. Thoothukudi – Tamil Nadu (TN)

Objective: The portal aims to improve transparency, facilitate industry collaboration and promote Ease of Doing Business (EoDB) in India’s maritime sector. Key Beneficiaries: Shipyards, ship repair facilities, equipment manufacturers, design agencies, classification societies, research and training institutions, financiers, insurers and regulators. MoU Between CSL and Damen: During the conclave, Cochin Shipyard Limited (CSL) signed an MoU with the Netherlands- based Damen Shipyards Group to explore opportunities for cooperation in shipbuilding, particularly the localisation and construction of specialised vessels in India. Signatories: The agreement was signed by Jose VJ, Chairman and Managing Director (CMD) of CSL; and Dingeman Van Woerden, Regional Sales Director (Asia), Damen Shipyards Group. Key Areas of Collaboration: Both organisations will explore opportunities for developing and constructing specialised vessels, including tugs and other technologically advanced vessels, in India. • The partnership will also focus on technology cooperation, knowledge sharing and the exchange of technical expertise. Key Targets: The Government of India (GoI) aims to become one of the world’s top 10 shipbuilding nations by 2030 and among the top 5 by 2047. India’s Active Shipbuilding Order Pipeline: While addressing the event, Union Minister Sonowal highlighted that India’s active shipbuilding order pipeline comprises more than 150 vessels valued at over USD 1.7 billion, with export orders representing more than 80% of the total value. About Third Advance Estimates 2025–26: Overview: The estimates were prepared by the Department of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare (DA&FW) under MoAFW, based on information received from States, Union Territories (UTs) and other government agencies. Area Covered: The total area under horticultural crops, i.e. fruits and vegetables in 2025-26 is estimated at approximately 297.21 lakh hectares (ha), slight reduction from 301.36 lakh ha in 2024-25. Fruit Production: Fruit production is estimated to rise from 1,176.49 LT in 2024-25 to 1,230.66 LT in 2025-26, an increase of 54.18 LT or 4.60%. • This increased output is attributed to better production of banana, mango, papaya, apple, pomegranate and jackfruit. Vegetable Production: Vegetable production is projected to rise by 4.35%, from 2,177.97 LT in 2024-25 to 2,272.68 LT in 2025-26. • The area under vegetables is estimated to increase from 117.91 lakh ha to 119.31 lakh ha. Growth Contributors: The increase is primarily driven by higher production of potato, tomato, brinjal, bottle gourd, cucumber, cabbage, beans and peas. • Potato: Production is estimated at 655.70 LT, registering an increase of 11.95% from 585.71 LT in the previous year. • Tomato: Production is projected to rise from 205.99 LT to 214.11 LT. • Onion: Production is estimated at 288.96 LT. Flower Production: Production is expected to grow by around 14.5%, reaching 48.82 LT in 2025-26, compared to 42.65 LT in 2024-25. • The area dedicated to flower cultivation has also risen to 4.10 lakh ha. Plantation crops: This estimate highlighted an increase in both the area and production of plantation crops, including arecanut, coconut, cashew, betel leaves and cocoa. • The production is estimated to increase by 7.56% to 182.64 LT. Medicinal Plants: Production of aromatic and medicinal plants is also expected to rise from 9.01 LT to 9.28 LT. Spices: The total area under spices in 2025-26 is estimated at 47.56 lakh ha, with production projected at 123.54 LT.
